one_sentence_story: In 1978 at CUNY's library photocopier, Ellen Langer proved that on small 5-page favors, an empty tautology ('because I have to make copies') boosted line-cutting yeses from 60% to 93% via scripted 'mindlessness' — yet on costly 20-page favors, only a genuine reason worked (42% vs 24%).
so_what_for_you: Two rules for Monday morning: (1) Always attach a real, specific **'because...'** when asking busy colleagues for help; (2) Whenever someone asks YOU for time or money, mentally cover the word 'because' and check whether the second half actually says anything.

jargon_map.plain: a grammatically complete 'reason' clause ('because I have to make copies') that adds zero new facts yet satisfies a polite social script
jargon_map.analogy: a sugar pill made out of grammar

jargon_map.plain: relying on overlearned social templates ('Polite Ask + Because = Say Yes') during low-cost moments instead of parsing every word

jargon_map.plain: Langer's built-in proof that rising effort cost (20 pages) shuts off mindless autopilot (93% to 24%) and turns on genuine argument scrutiny (42%)
jargon_map.analogy: waking up the security guard when the bill exceeds $5

jargon_map.plain: actively noticing novel distinctions in the present context rather than running yesterday's script
